passages.title: A – Street Photography Day
passages.text: Spend Saturday exploring the old town with professional photographer Dan Mills. You will learn how to take interesting pictures of people and buildings in busy streets. Please bring your own digital camera, as phones are not suitable for the techniques we practise. Beginners are welcome. The £35 price includes lunch in a local café.

passages.title: B – Painting in the Hills
passages.text: This two-day course takes place entirely outdoors in the beautiful Hadley Hills. Each morning we walk about three kilometres to a new spot, then spend the day painting the views. No experience is needed, and all paints, brushes and paper are provided. Accommodation is not included, but the organisers can suggest places to stay nearby.

passages.title: C – A Taste of Italy
passages.text: This Sunday afternoon class is for people who already feel confident in the kitchen and want to discover real Italian home cooking. Chef Paola teaches no more than eight students at a time, so everyone gets plenty of attention. Several dishes are made without meat, and at the end you sit down together to enjoy what you have cooked.

passages.title: D – Kitchen Basics
passages.text: Never cooked before? On this Saturday morning course you will learn simple skills such as chopping vegetables safely, making sauces and baking bread. It is a great chance for families to learn together: children aged ten and over are welcome if they come with an adult. You take all the recipes home so that you can practise.

passages.title: E – Photos with Your Phone
passages.text: You don't need an expensive camera to take great pictures. This relaxed Sunday course shows beginners how to get the best from the camera on their mobile phone. We start indoors with the basics, then practise in the park. After the course, you can send your photos to the teacher by email and get personal advice.

passages.title: F – Pottery Weekend
passages.text: Spend Saturday and Sunday in our bright studio learning to make bowls and cups on the potter's wheel. Clay, tools and aprons are all provided, and no experience is needed. Your pieces will be fired in our special oven and will be ready to collect two weeks later. Lunch and drinks are included in the price.

passages.title: G – Write Your Own Songs
passages.text: If you have always wanted to write the words for songs, join singer-songwriter Amy Cole at the Riverside Arts Centre this Saturday. You'll learn how to find ideas and make your lines rhyme. At the end of the day, the group will perform some of the songs in front of friends and family. Musical instruments are not necessary.

passages.title: H – The Home Story Club
passages.text: Join our creative writing course from your own home. On Sunday mornings we meet by video call to discuss short stories and learn how to create interesting characters. Between sessions, you write your own story and share it with the group. At the end of the course, the best stories are printed in a small book.

questions.question: Laura would like to learn to take better photos, but she only has a mobile phone. She works every Saturday, and she would like someone to comment on her pictures after the course has finished.
questions.explanation: Photos with Your Phone is on Sunday, teaches people to use 'the camera on their mobile phone', and 'after the course, you can send your photos to the teacher by email and get personal advice'. Street Photography Day is also about photos, but it is on Saturday, when Laura works, and you must 'bring your own digital camera, as phones are not suitable'.

questions.question: Tom has hardly ever cooked, and he would like to learn together with his twelve-year-old daughter. They are only free on Saturday mornings.
questions.explanation: Kitchen Basics is 'for families to learn together', accepts 'children aged ten and over' with an adult, is for people who have 'never cooked before' and takes place on Saturday morning. A Taste of Italy is also a cooking class, but it is on Sunday afternoon and is for people who 'already feel confident in the kitchen'.

questions.question: Maria has been cooking for years and wants to learn to make dishes from another country. She doesn't eat meat, and she prefers learning in a small group where the teacher has time for everyone.
questions.explanation: A Taste of Italy is for people who 'already feel confident in the kitchen', teaches 'real Italian home cooking', has 'no more than eight students' so 'everyone gets plenty of attention', and 'several dishes are made without meat'. Kitchen Basics is also about cooking, but it is for people who have 'never cooked before' and does not teach food from another country.

questions.question: James wants to try painting for the first time and doesn't own any equipment. He would like to spend the whole weekend outside, and he enjoys walking.
questions.explanation: Painting in the Hills is a 'two-day course' that 'takes place entirely outdoors', includes a walk of 'about three kilometres' each morning, needs 'no experience', and 'all paints, brushes and paper are provided'. Pottery Weekend also lasts two days, needs no experience and provides everything, but it is held 'in our bright studio', not outside, and it is not painting.

questions.question: Sophie loves writing and wants to improve her stories. She has a young baby, so she can't leave the house, and she would love to see her writing printed one day.
questions.explanation: The Home Story Club can be done 'from your own home' by video call, is about 'short stories', and 'the best stories are printed in a small book'. Write Your Own Songs is also a writing course, but it is held at the Riverside Arts Centre, so Sophie would have to leave the house, and the songs are performed, not printed.
